heading: 7.2 Storage
text:
### 7.2 Storage [LUNI.7.2]

A unit-typed field is stored in the **base unit** of its dimension, regardless of
which unit was declared. `temp: fahrenheit` stores values as kelvin (float64) per
§4.1 (`base kelvin` for the temperature dimension). `distance: kilometer` stores
as meters (float64). `duration: millisecond` stores as nanoseconds (int64).

**Float→int storage cast** (§17.5): when a `float64` value lands in a
field whose dimension declares `storage int64` (notably the `time` dimension,
§4.1), the cast uses IEEE 754 `roundTiesToEven` to avoid ±1-quantum drift across
platforms. Conversion formulas (`unit formula`, §4.5) that produce a `float64`
result destined for `int64` storage — `hz_to_period(x) = 1e9 / x` is the
canonical example — apply the same rule at the final cast.
